candidate_name: CSF over-drainage prevention via venous-pressure-aware regulation
territory_of_origin: CV-T04 (Venous-aware regulation) — reopened as a new problem-first discovery

computational_conclusion.reasoning: When the hydraulic simulation is reconstructed with consistent equations (dP(t) = ICP(t) - P_venous(t) enforced at every time step) and the actual eShunt valve specification (proportional, ~10 mL/h at <=8 mmHg gradient, per published eShunt description — NOT a binary check valve with a 7 mmHg threshold), the model predicts a SAFE equilibrium ICP of 10.34 mmHg when the patient stands. This is within the safe range (5-15 mmHg). The proportional valve limits flow as ICP drops, reaching a safe equilibrium. The hypothesis H is KILLED under the corrected model.

key_model_parameters.valve_type: proportional pressure-driven slit valve (NOT binary check valve)

real_world_conclusion.reasoning: The computational kill does NOT prove that no real-world over-drainage phenomenon exists. It proves that the CURRENT SOURCE-BOUND HYDRAULIC MODEL does not predict dangerous over-drainage at equilibrium. The model uses: (1) a linear proportional valve law derived from a single published performance point (~10 mL/h at <=8 mmHg) — the actual valve curve may be nonlinear; (2) modeled P_venous values (8 mmHg supine, 2 mmHg standing) that need clinical measurement; (3) a generic CSF compliance (10 mL/mmHg) that varies by patient. Real-world over-drainage in eShunt patients could still occur due to: patient-specific valve characteristics, nonlinear valve behavior at high gradients, transient dynamics not captured by the equilibrium analysis, or patient populations with different compliance. The model killed the hypothesis within its domain of validity. It did NOT declare reality nonexistent outside that domain.
what_would_change_this: Clinical measurement of actual P_venous variation in eShunt patients (not modeled values)
Full valve characteristic curve (not a single performance point)
Long-term (>90 day) STRIDE data on over-drainage complications
Transient analysis of posture transitions (not just equilibrium)

model_failure_history.model_used: Binary check valve with 7 mmHg threshold
model_failure_history.prediction: Catastrophic over-drainage: ICP crashes to 0.8 mmHg, Q = 1.2 mL/min
model_failure_history.apparent_breakthrough: The model appeared to show a clinically dangerous over-drainage phenomenon that no existing technology addressed
model_failure_history.error: The model was WRONG. The eShunt valve is NOT a binary check valve with a 7 mmHg threshold. The published eShunt description says the valve is PROPORTIONAL (~10 mL/h at <=8 mmHg). The binary model produced uncontrolled flow once the threshold was exceeded, which does not match the actual device behavior. Additionally, the pressure equations did not reconcile: dP was reported as 7 when ICP-P_venous = 18.7, and as 13 when ICP-P_venous = -1.2. The values from different simulation phases (initial vs equilibrium) were mixed in the same causal chain.
model_failure_history.lesson: A wrong valve model can produce an apparent invention opportunity that does not exist. Always source-bind the valve specification before running the simulation. Always enforce dP = ICP - P_venous at every time step.

model_failure_history.model_used: Proportional valve with source-bound ~10 mL/h at <=8 mmHg, linear model
model_failure_history.prediction: Safe equilibrium: ICP = 10.34 mmHg, Q = 10.4 mL/h (within safe range)
model_failure_history.result: HYPOTHESIS KILLED — the corrected model does not predict dangerous over-drainage
model_failure_history.lesson: When the model is corrected, the invention opportunity may disappear. The machine must kill the problem honestly rather than preserving it because a mechanism would be interesting.

adversarial_regression_test.test_description: This case is a permanent regression test against model-induced invention hallucination. The machine must NEVER use a wrong model to manufacture an invention opportunity. The test verifies that: (1) the valve model is source-bound before simulation; (2) dP = ICP - P_venous is enforced at every time step; (3) the simulation distinguishes INITIAL / TRANSIENT / EQUILIBRIUM phases; (4) the hypothesis is killed if the corrected model does not predict the phenomenon.
test_steps: 1. Verify the valve model is source-bound (not assumed binary with arbitrary threshold)
2. Verify dP(t) = ICP(t) - P_venous(t) at every time step (dP_check == dP)
3. Verify INITIAL / TRANSIENT / EQUILIBRIUM phases are labeled and not mixed
4. Verify the 816 mL/day extrapolation is NOT present (transient flow cannot be treated as constant)
5. Verify the hypothesis is KILLED if the corrected model predicts safe equilibrium
6. Verify the cemetery record distinguishes computational kill from real-world disproval
adversarial_regression_test.test_input: The Round 37 binary check valve model with 7 mmHg threshold
adversarial_regression_test.expected_output: The model produces apparent over-drainage (ICP = 0.8, Q = 1.2) but this is WRONG because the actual valve is proportional
adversarial_regression_test.test_output: The corrected proportional model produces safe equilibrium (ICP = 10.34, Q = 0.174) — hypothesis killed

cemetery_entry.candidate: OVF-001: Over-drainage prevention via venous-pressure-aware regulation
cemetery_entry.death_cause: KILLED_BY_CORRECTED_HYDRAULIC_MODEL — the existing eShunt proportional valve neutralizes the over-drainage problem at equilibrium
cemetery_entry.reopenable: conditional — reopenable only if: (1) clinical data shows real-world over-drainage in eShunt patients despite the model prediction, OR (2) the actual valve characteristic curve is found to be significantly different from the linear model, OR (3) a specific patient population is identified where the model assumptions do not hold
cemetery_entry.anti_resurrection_rule: Do NOT reopen OVF-001 based on a model change alone. The model already killed it. Reopening requires CLINICAL evidence that the model prediction is wrong — not a different model.
cemetery_entry.permanent_lesson: A model can kill a hypothesis inside its domain of validity. It cannot declare reality nonexistent outside that domain. The computational kill is strong but does NOT prove real-world over-drainage is impossible. Future invention work must distinguish these two conclusions.
